title: Alien vs Predator
subtitle: Three ways into the same nightmare
summary: Alien vs Predator is Rebellion's first-person game for the Atari Jaguar, released in October 1994.
body: Alien vs Predator is Rebellion's first-person game for the Atari Jaguar, released in October 1994. Its three scenarios place an Alien, a Predator or a Colonial Marine inside the infested Golgotha base. The same corridors support different objectives and abilities, changing the meaning of an encounter according to the creature being controlled. The base connects five levels through elevators and air ducts, creating a place to learn and navigate while its inhabitants turn every journey between rooms into a threat.

As Marine Lance J. Lewis, the player begins without weapons or security clearance and must assemble the means to escape. Fallen soldiers provide guns, ammunition and access cards, while terminals reveal information about the base. The motion tracker becomes another tool for reading dangers beyond the immediate view. Reaching the self-destruct mechanism and finding an escape pod gives exploration a practical purpose. Each newly opened door may advance that plan, but also increases the area in which supplies and a safe route must be remembered.

The Alien travels through air ducts and fights with claws, jaw and tail. It prepares future bodies by infecting Marines, turning a successful attack into a possible return after death. The Predator instead hunts for the Alien queen's skull and gains weapons through an honor-based score: killing while invisible can cost progress. Its camouflage and vision filters offer different ways to read a room. These changes extend beyond the appearance of the weapon, making each scenario a distinct relationship with the same hostile architecture.
